_note: Classification rules for the existing Python foundation, frozen. Generated from tools/kinglet_spike/inventory.py and pinned to it by tests/kinglet_spike/test_foundation_inventory.py. The inventory reads this tree and never writes to it; no source file is deleted, ported or rewritten by 00D.

rules.why: Fixture data is runtime-neutral; every candidate reads the same canonical shapes.

rules.disposition: keep if python wins, otherwise adapt
rules.why: A behavioural test is a migration ASSET: its assertions are the only written specification of what the builder does. It is never `replace`, and never retired without parity.

rules.disposition: keep if python wins, otherwise replace
rules.why: Packaging entry point only. No behaviour survives the move, so `replace` is honest -- but only with every current test module named as the parity suite.

rules.disposition: keep if python wins, otherwise retire-after-parity
rules.why: Implementation behaviour must exist in the winner and be proved equivalent before retirement. Every current test module is named.
Canonical data consumed by the builder. No runtime choice touches it; marking it for migration would be busywork with risk.
Not inventoried at all. Discovery comes from `git ls-files`, so exclusion is by construction rather than by a filter someone must remember to widen.
